components.name: Primary Button

narrative.overview: The game reads like a well-travelled atlas: a deep lagoon teal for the instruments, sunbaked terracotta for anything you press, and pale mint and sea-glass for land and water. The map is the main subject, and everything around it (the game bar, the menus, the celebration screens) stays calm so the player's eye can go back to the map. Surfaces are flat colour fields with no shadows; depth comes from tone. Shapes are round and friendly, like pills, soft cards and layered waves, so the game feels welcoming without being childish. Playfulness comes from motion and sound (confetti, emojis, sound effects) rather than from decoration on the chrome. Light and dark modes are equally important. Dark mode is a night sea, not an inverted page: teal goes deeper, the land turns to slate and the ocean to dark blue-green.
keyCharacteristics: The map dominates; chrome is a thin frame of flat colour.
Two voices: teal for structure, terracotta for action.
Round shapes: pill buttons, 16px cards, wave dividers.
Flat at rest; depth through tonal layering.
Every colour has a light and a dark value.

rules.name: The Terracotta Means Press Rule
rules.body: Terracotta is reserved for things the player acts on and for progress toward the goal. Structure never uses it.

rules.name: The Token-Only Rule
rules.body: Colours come from the semantic tokens in theme/system.ts, read through colorVar() or the Chakra CSS variables. Components never hard-code hex values, so both modes stay in sync.

rules.name: The Found Country Rule
rules.body: A found country is always marked with Shallow Water, which is also what hover and press resolve to on micro-countries, so the map reads as "found" at a glance.

rules.name: The Country Is the Headline Rule
rules.body: During a run, the target country is the only display-size text on screen.

rules.name: The Flat Atlas Rule
rules.body: Surfaces have no shadow at rest. To separate a layer, change its tone, not its elevation.

dos: Do read every colour from a semantic token with a light and a dark value (theme/system.ts, colorVar()).
Do use Sunbaked Terracotta pills for every primary action.
Do keep the game chrome flat and let the map carry the screen.
Do keep touch targets large enough for a finger, including micro-countries.
Do design both light and dark modes together.
donts: Don't hard-code hex values in components.
Don't add shadows to separate surfaces; change the tone.
Don't use terracotta for structural chrome or decoration.
Don't put display-size text on the game screen other than the target country.
